- [LFAC.1.2.2] **Retract-and-replace** on each meaningful
  change. Exactly one live fact per identity key — the
  slots the `logical` schema declares `key` per [LFAC.1.7].
  (This is the key-subset case of the declared-key model.)

idris.name: ltim_2_8_6__entered_is_stamped
idris.note: The replacement of a retract-and-replace is an assert that changed working memory, and is stamped with the sample at which it entered.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_6__restamp
idris.note: Retract-and-replace on the stamps: the replaced fact's row goes with it (it is no longer live) and the replacement is stamped at the sample it entered.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_6__three_asserts
idris.note: The replacement at 8, executed: the new fact stamped 8, the old id without a row.

idris.name: Lfac_1_2_2__fresh_for
idris.note: What a fact about to enter working memory must not clash with, by its kind's lifecycle: under the entity lifecycle no live fact of its kind and key; under the others nothing.

idris.name: Lfac_1_2_2__unique
idris.note: ONE LIVE FACT PER IDENTITY KEY for every kind under the entity lifecycle -- the key-subset case of [LFAC.1.7.2]: two live facts of one such kind with one key are one fact.

idris.name: iret_11_4__run_unique
idris.note: A RUN keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: iret_11_4__step_unique
idris.note: ONE FIRING keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_unique
idris.note: ASSERT UNDER THE LIFECYCLE keeps one live fact per key: an entity assert that finds nothing inserts the only fact of its key; one that finds a different value retracts the one fact of its key, then inserts; the other lifecycles never insert an entity. The clause's retract-and-replace, as an invariant.

idris.name: iret_19_1__insert_unique
idris.note: Inserting a fresh fact keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: iret_19_2__retract_unique
idris.note: Retracting keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: lfac_1_2_2__append_unique
idris.note: Appending a fact fresh for its kind's lifecycle keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: lfac_1_2_2__clash
idris.note: A fresh fact clashes with no live fact: under the entity lifecycle by freshness, under the others because no fact of its kind is an entity.

idris.name: lfac_1_2_2__remove_unique
idris.note: Removing facts keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: lfac_1_7_2__one_live
idris.note: ONE LIVE FACT: two live facts of a singleton kind are one fact, from one live fact per key.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__boundary_unique
idris.note: One input pumped keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__replay_unique
idris.note: EVERY HISTORY keeps one live fact per identity key.

idris.name: lnls_5_1__j_max_1
idris.note: The clause's one-live-fact-per-key is what makes J_max = 1 under the anchor.

idris.name: lnls_5_1__j_max_1_after_history
idris.note: THEOREM 5, closed at the top: after any history from a loaded network, at every node whose join test is a full-key anchor on an entity-lifecycle kind, every token joins at most one fact of the node's memory. The clause's left-activation half. Its right-activation half -- exactly one left-memory token per key -- needs every pattern of the prefix anchored, not only the right one: with a pattern of the prefix unconstrained by the anchor, tokens differing in that pattern share the key.

idris.name: lscp_2_1_1__withdraw_unique
idris.note: WITHDRAW keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_4__apply_unique
idris.note: AN INPUT keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_7__do_action_unique
idris.note: ONE RHS ACTION keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_7__do_actions_unique
idris.note: The RHS keeps uniqueness.

idris.name: rdsc_4a_5__load_unique
idris.note: The loaded network's empty working memory is unique.
